pr_body:
Closes #72625. Approved API details: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/72625#issuecomment-1238477596.

`DrainToImmutable` will "do the cheapest thing possible" to return the current contents as an immutable array and then reset the collection to a zero-length array.

issue_context.title: [API Proposal]: `ImmutableArray<T>.Builder.ToImmutableAndClear()`
comments:
I also use something like this quite often in my generators and would very much welcome this API 🙂

Nit: the proposal says `ToImmutableAndClear` but the example uses `ToImmutableAndFree`, old snippet?

> Nit: the proposal says ToImmutableAndClear but the example uses ToImmutableAndFree, old snippet?

No, force of habit. Roslyn also pools builders.
Sounds useful enough. If we do add such a method, we might want to explicitly document that any perf benefits are predicated on `Capacity == Count`.

review_comments: May have missed it, but is there a test here that calls DrainToImmutable on an empty builder?

There were tests that covered that indirectly by draining after clearing or previously draining. I'm adding 2 more tests that will explicitly cover the scenarios of a fully empty builder; thanks for the suggestion.
Literally every use of `var` added in this file in this change is against style guidelines, and should (have) be(en) expanded to the target type.

Yes... but as with Microsoft.Extensions, the whole project started off with a team with different coding guidelines, and we haven't gone through and made them all conform to ours, at which point we've generally opted for new code in the file to conform to the style used by the rest of the file.

Thanks, and yeah, I did intentionally follow the patterns in the file/project per our [contributing dos and don'ts](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#dos-and-donts).

> **DO** follow our coding style (C# code-specific).
> 
> **DO** give priority to the current style of the project or file you're changing even if it diverges from the general guidelines.
